subject: Pull / work-stealing coordination Phases 0-3 (dark) — PR #1550

new_internal_endpoints: GET /api/internal/next-task (dual-auth: internal secret OR agent scoped key + pilot-allowlist gate)
POST /api/internal/tasks/{execution_id}/result (dual-auth: internal secret OR agent scoped key owning the execution)
attack_surface.network_topology_change: none (worker reaches backend HTTP API only, same as heartbeat/#1083)

findings.title: Cross-tenant execution-existence enumeration oracle on the pull result seam
findings.description: POST /api/internal/tasks/{execution_id}/result returns 404 for a non-existent execution but 403 for an execution that exists but belongs to a different agent. This 404-then-403 differential in one handler violates Trinity's self-uniform enumeration-safety invariant (#186, regression-tested by test_186_enumeration_uniformity.py) and deviates from the #1083 callback (src/backend/routers/agents.py:1045) it claims to mirror, which folds both cases into a uniform 404.
findings.exploit_scenario: An attacker holding any valid agent-scoped MCP key (a compromised pilot agent, or an exfiltrated TRINITY_MCP_API_KEY) POSTs to /api/internal/tasks/<id>/result with their key. 403 => <id> is a real execution owned by some other agent; 404 => it does not exist. Reachable against ALL executions (get_execution reads the whole schedule_executions table, populated by schedules/webhooks/chat/loops) and even with pull-mode fully OFF (the result endpoint's auth is inline, NOT gated on the is_pull_pilot_agent allowlist that /next-task uses; the router is mounted unconditionally at main.py:937).
findings.impact: LOW. Cross-tenant existence confirmation for execution_ids the attacker already possesses via a side channel. NOT brute-forceable: execution_ids are 128-bit secrets.token_urlsafe(16), so the id space cannot be enumerated. Invariant #186 was written for low-entropy agent names; for 128-bit ids the practical disclosure is minimal — hence LOW, not the usual MEDIUM for an enumeration oracle.
findings.recommendation:
Merge the two checks into a uniform 404, mirroring agents.py:1045:
    execution = db.get_execution(execution_id)
    if execution is None or not heartbeat_service.authorize_heartbeat(key, execution.agent_name):
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Execution not found")
One-line fix; makes the handler self-uniform and consistent with the mirrored #1083 endpoint.

positive_notes: SECURITY IMPROVEMENT: the pull seams use the agent's OWN scoped MCP key (dual-auth) instead of injecting the master INTERNAL_API_SECRET into pilot containers (the prior design). A compromised pilot can only claim/report for itself, never reach the other /api/internal/* endpoints (least privilege, #307/#1159).
claim_token is secrets.token_urlsafe(32) = 256-bit; the result CAS gates on token match + status precondition + ownership, so a stale/wrong-token/cross-agent result cannot clobber a terminal.
Worker-uploaded result content is passed through sanitize_response / sanitize_execution_log before persistence (no credential leakage into stored results).

clean_phases.P2_secrets: No secret values or personal paths in the committed diff; planning docs genericized (no pay-widget path / API key).
clean_phases.P5_infra: New compose vars (PULL_MODE_PILOT_AGENTS / MAX_REDELIVERY) are non-secret with placeholder/default values; no new Redis/network exposure; agent network reach unchanged.
clean_phases.P7_ai: No user input into system prompts introduced; result content sanitized; no master secret injected into agents.
clean_phases.P9_A03_injection: All new pull SQL uses SQLAlchemy Core bound params; the one raw text() sweep binds :status + literal IS NULL. No string-interpolated SQL. worker_id is stored as a bound value (no SQLi; log-injection excluded).

trend: New finding (no prior report covers the pull endpoints). Prior cso-diff reports audited other branches.
